slices.focus: Fall cohort attrition tests the new support system, forcing late-night calls and protocol design
slices.summary: The fall first-year cohort hits a rough patch as overtime, transportation failures, and shame spirals cause multiple apprentices to miss evening classes. Derek spends nights making personal calls — to apprentices, a parent, and a foreman — trying to catch people before they disappear completely. Ron Belski uses the wobbles to needle him that the support model is failing, which gets under Derek's skin. He decides to build a formal one-page contact protocol (who gets contacted when, what gets documented, when contractor/family contacts get involved) and a blunt three-point reset talk for class, while acknowledging he needs to protect his own sleep.
open_loops: Drafting a one-page contact ladder protocol with message scripts
Designing a blunt three-point reset talk about calling early
Talking to contractors about not running first-years late on class nights when avoidable
Building a timed contact sequence (same-night, next-day, escalate) for silent cases
Protecting sleep from the mental replay of missing apprentices
